definitions.explanation: An indefinite span of several decades. Formed from {何|なん} (how many) plus {十年|じゅうねん}, it states that the number of decades is large or unknown rather than asking for it.

examples.japanese: {何十年|なんじゅうねん}も{前|まえ}の{話|はなし}だ。
この{寺|てら}は{何十年|なんじゅうねん}にも{渡|わた}って{守|まも}られてきた。
examples.english: This temple has been looked after for decades.

examples.japanese: {何十年|なんじゅうねん}{働|はたら}いても{家|いえ}が{買|か}えないという{声|こえ}が{若|わか}い{世代|せだい}から{上|あ}がっている。
examples.english: Young people are saying that even decades of work won't buy them a house.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always followed by も, which supplies the sense of "as many as." Without も the phrase reads as a genuine question — {何十年|なんじゅうねん}かかりますか (how many decades will it take?).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {何十年|なんじゅうねん}も{前|まえ}: decades ago
- {何十年|なんじゅうねん}ぶり: for the first time in decades
- {何十年|なんじゅうねん}にも{渡|わた}って: over the course of decades

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {数十年|すうじゅうねん}: several decades — the written, more measured equivalent
- {何年|なんねん}も: for many years — a smaller, vaguer span
